---
title: Decisions
subtitle: Questions the agent is not allowed to settle, and how the owner settled
  them
toc: true
---

The brief lists the decisions that belong to a human: physics modelling choices, licence and
data questions, which properties to prove, use of the compute cluster, and benchmark failures
that aren't explained by a bug. When the agent reaches one, it writes the question down with
context and a recommended answer, carries on with whatever isn't blocked, and waits. Numbers
(OQ-*n*) match the project's internal record. Newest first within each group.

## Awaiting a decision

### OQ-43 · Grid check for the JOREK case (b) growth rates {#oq-43}

Awaiting a decision on how to check the case (b) growth rates against grid resolution. A
from-scratch check on the doubled grid costs far more than the approved compute, because
these modes rise slowly from round-off. The options are: the grid check on case (a)'s two
faster pedestal modes, with case (b) reported as converged in time step only (recommended);
a long chain of case (b) jobs; a JOREK patch to carry a mode across grids; or the time-step
check alone.

## Settled

### OQ-42 · MAST-U closed-loop check after the projected reference stopped {#oq-42}

*Decided 25 Oct 2026.* Limited MAST-U scope. The one projected-reference run of [OQ-38](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-38) stopped
on its own 1 gB rule, and a read-only screen of the 40 saved states shows that the rule cannot
complete on this scenario ([150 negative raw heat diffusivities at 19 faces; 46 would reach the 1 gB stop, at 31 of 40 states, the first at state 1]{.claim}[C-240](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-240){.cid .st-measured}). The MAST-U comparison against a TGLF
reference trajectory is recorded as not evaluable, and MAST-U is certified at the M4 review
with that limitation stated ([K-030](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-030), [K-032](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-032)). ITER's measured pass stands. The model, guard,
acceptance limits and frozen splits are unchanged, and no further MAST-U reference compute is
planned. Options not taken: redefining the comparison against the guarded TGLF/fallback
hybrid, which would still fail the limit on the descriptive distance ([T_e 32.0%, T_i 41.5% on the 14 faces where both serve TGLF, against the 15% limit]{.claim}[C-242](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-242){.cid .st-measured}),
and raising the stop threshold, when projected magnitudes reach thousands of gB.

### OQ-41 · Core and axis modes hide the pedestal in the JOREK n-scan {#oq-41}

*Decided 25 Oct 2026.* In case (a), quote pedestal growth rates only where the pedestal mode
is the fastest mode (n = 12, 16), and report the other n as "not measured: core or axis mode
faster". Close case (a) on the time-step check: n = 12 and 16 are "converged in Δt, grid not
checked", not quotable ([n = 12: 0.04397 → 0.04397 (−0.01%); n = 16: 0.03744 → 0.03633 (−2.94%); both within the 5% tolerance]{.claim}[C-227](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-227){.cid .st-measured}). Move to case (b), the TORAX state, where the
core q minimum is higher, and run the full convergence check there. Compute: up to five
one-node jobs of at most six hours for case (b), each announced before submission. Options
not taken: damping the core with ψ-dependent dissipation (which `model303` doesn't support
without a source patch), changing the case (a) core, and running the case (a) grid check
now.

### OQ-40 · Reconciling the TORAX state with a JOREK equilibrium {#oq-40}

*Decided 25 Oct 2026.* TORAX evolves the current on a fixed geometry, so its state is not a
Grad–Shafranov equilibrium, and JOREK's equilibrium from TORAX's pressure and current misses
the q and current tolerance. Use that equilibrium with FF′ multiplied by one factor so that
the plasma current equals TORAX's. Acceptance: current within 1%, and pressure as TORAX's by
construction. The q difference from TORAX is reported as a known inconsistency
([median q difference +10.7% (psi_N 0.1–0.5), +3.2% (0.5–0.9), −4.9% (0.9–0.95); q95 4.64 against 4.89, q_min 1.84 against 1.64]{.claim}[C-235](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-235){.cid .st-measured}). Options not taken: tuning FF′ until q matches, which changes the
current profile, and building a self-consistent free-boundary TORAX state first.

### OQ-39 · Physics settings for the first JOREK stability runs {#oq-39}

*Decided 16 Oct 2026.* Case (a), the EQDSK as given, first; then case (b), the TORAX state.
Before any stability run, the equilibrium must match its source: q within 2% over normalised
flux 0.1–0.95 and plasma current within 1%, starting with the separatrix as boundary
([I_p −0.93%, largest q difference 1.1%, q 4.668 against 4.668 at psi_N 0.95: passes the tolerance of q within 2% and I_p within 1%]{.claim}[C-221](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-221){.cid .st-measured}). Model `model303` with diamagnetic terms, with full MHD later as a
one-n cross-check. Spitzer resistivity, temperature-dependent, with viscosity at Prandtl
number about 1; enhanced resistivity only as a scan, if resolution demands it. Toroidal mode
numbers 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 16, 20, one per run. Unstable means a positive growth rate with
diamagnetic terms; ω* and the EPED-like ratio are reported too. A growth rate is quoted only
if halving the time step and doubling the radial and poloidal resolution each change it by at
most 5%. Compute: up to three one-node jobs of at most six hours, each announced.

### OQ-38 · Standard-settings MAST-U reference {#oq-38}

*Decided 16 Oct 2026.* The MAST-U reference for the closed-loop check is TGLF at its standard
settings, the convention that labelled all training data ([K-032](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-032)). In the reference only,
negative raw heat diffusivities are set to zero instead of sending the face to the fallback;
every projection is logged, and the run stops if any projected heat-flux magnitude reaches
1 gB. The production surrogate, raw guard and acceptance limits are unchanged. One run was
approved. It stopped on the 1 gB rule and saved no trajectory; [OQ-42](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-42) records what followed.

### OQ-37 · Scope of a JOREK integration {#oq-37}

*Decided 16 Oct 2026.* Use JOREK as an external open-source (Tier A) MHD reference,
run outside the JAX loop and never a runtime dependency of a surrogate. First use:
linear pedestal-stability scans over toroidal mode number on ITER hybrid, then an
internal-kink check of the sawtooth trigger, then MAST-U. Build the sparse solver
ourselves; one short CPU job to repeat JOREK's regression cases and measure step cost.
Nonlinear ELM runs are later reference runs; disruption studies are deferred. Log
entries reporting JOREK work are public and acknowledge the JOREK team.

### OQ-22 · Properties, coverage and tolerances for verification {#oq-22}

*Decided 11 Oct 2026.* M4 proves properties of the surrogates over input boxes, calibrates
their uncertainty and compares closed-loop trajectories with the physics codes; the brief
leaves the choice of properties to the owner.

**Decision.** The owner accepted the agent's recommendations. Transport: heat flux
non-decreasing in its temperature gradient, certified output bounds over the training box, and
local robustness on sub-boxes around the loop's states. EC: certified bounds of current, centres
and widths per launcher, and the heating centre moving by at most 0.05 for input changes of one
percent of their ranges. ITER pedestal: certified bounds of pressure and width around the ITER
states TORAX visits. Calibrated intervals with 90% coverage. Closed-loop tolerances: transport
within 15% of TGLF on the radii the surrogate serves, EC within 10% of GENRAY on sampled loop
states. The original verification tool was alpha,beta-CROWN on checked PyTorch copies;
[OQ-24](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-24) selects auto_LiRPA with input splitting instead.


### OQ-21 · RF and pedestal references {#oq-21}

*Decided 10 Oct 2026.* Reference, model and channel
choices were recorded on 8 Oct: GENRAY for EC heating and current drive, and the pretrained
EPEDNN network for the ITER pedestal. The prescribed MAST-U pedestal remains, with predictive
closure deferred; IC is deferred. A bounded numerical pilot of the original ITER deck
completed ([the corrected EC reference completes in 83.16 s with readable native profiles]{.claim}[C-156](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-156){.cid .st-measured}).

**Question (8 Oct).** How do the reference outputs become labels and TORAX inputs: the
current-drive method, heating channels, the current definition and its sign, the radial
mapping, the pedestal branch, temperature split, density, pedestal-top location and the
fallbacks; and what to label first.

**Decision (10 Oct).** The owner accepted the agent's recommendations as written. EC: the
deck's adjoint current drive, with the momentum-conserving method as a check on a few cases;
electron heating from both channels, kept separately; current as GENRAY's flux-surface average
of $j \cdot B$ over $B_0$, the same $B_0$ as TORAX's, signed positive along the plasma current;
a remap that keeps every cell's heating and current integrals; labels per MW injected; the
Gaussian EC model fitted to the labels as fallback; targets after a baseline. Pedestal: both
diamagnetic corrections, solution 0; equal ion and electron temperatures; the prescribed
density; top at one minus twice the half-width in poloidal flux, mapped through the
equilibrium; the prescribed pedestal as fallback. The first EC dataset samples ITER states from
the transport dataset's TORAX runs, with two launcher families
([entry 36](log/36-ec-and-pedestal-contracts.qmd)).

**Targets and [K-028](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-028) (10 Oct, later).** The owner accepted the recommended EC targets: absorbed
power and driven current within a median relative error of one tenth, heating centre within
0.05 in radius, on held-out runs. For [K-028](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-028) the owner chose to drop states whose current is
far from the equilibrium's, and approved compute for the structured model. The structured
EC surrogate meets all three targets ([entry 38](log/38-structured-ec-surrogate.qmd)).


### OQ-20 · Monotonicity where TGLF is not monotone; the ITER collisionality range {#oq-20}

*Decided 3 Oct 2026.* [OQ-19](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-19) asked for monotonicity in the gradients to be measured on TGLF
before it is imposed. On TGLF scans of $a/L_{T_e}$ and $a/L_{T_i}$ around v1 test points, the
heat flux falls along most scans ([falls somewhere in 77% (Q_e) and 80% (Q_i) of MAST-U scans, 51% and 74% of ITER scans; by more than half in 40% and 57% (MAST-U), 34% and 57% (ITER)]{.claim}[C-113](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-113){.cid .st-measured}), and the v1 ensemble's slope is negative at a
minority of test points ([entry 20](log/20-heat-flux-positivity-monotonicity.qmd)). Separately,
the approved ITER collisionality range excluded part of the ITER loop's radii from dataset v3,
and the guard rejects them ([K-023](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-023)). Two questions: (1) drop monotonicity as a requirement, or
impose it although TGLF is not monotone; (2) widen the ITER collisionality range.

**Decision.** (1) Monotonicity is a requirement for the TGLF surrogates: $Q_e$ non-decreasing in
$a/L_{T_e}$, $Q_i$ non-decreasing in $a/L_{T_i}$. Where TGLF decreases, the surrogate departs
from TGLF by construction; the departure is measured and reported as a ceiling, not hidden.
(2) The ITER collisionality range is widened for dataset v3 only; the M2 sampling space and the
v1 and v2 datasets are unchanged. The owner also approved the GPU retraining of the structured
variants and the cluster job that compares the surrogate with TGLF inside TORAX.

### OQ-19 · What to sample next, the accuracy target, and the sign of the heat flux {#oq-19}

*Decided 3 Oct 2026.* On the M2 datasets, a uniform box in 17 inputs, the surrogates' error
falls slowly with more data, and the first round of active learning gained nothing over
uniform points ([entry 19](log/19-active-learning-round-1.qmd)). The configuration had no
accuracy target. The brief asks for positivity, zero flux below threshold and monotonicity in
the gradients, while TGLF's own heat fluxes are negative in a minority of cases
([Q_e < 0 in 2.0-6.5% of cases (below -1 gB in 0.5-1.5%; median of the negative values -0.03 to -0.09 gB); Q_i < 0 in 9.4-14.1% (below -1 gB in 2.2-5.1%); particle fluxes negative in 33-54%]{.claim}[C-102](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-102){.cid .st-measured}). Three questions: (1) keep sampling the box, or sample elsewhere; (2) which
held-out target; (3) a ReLU on the heat-flux outputs (the owner's question).

**Decision.** The owner left (1) and (2) to the agent's recommendation, which stands, and asked
for (3).
(1) Dataset v3 per machine is sampled where the coupled simulation goes: TGLF inputs from
TORAX states along trajectories over a family of scenarios per machine, with the gradients and
kinetic inputs perturbed around each state and the geometry from the same equilibrium as the
profiles (this lifts [K-018](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-018) for v3). MAST-U profiles are simulated with TORAX on FreeGSNKE
MAST-U equilibria; no experimental data are used. v1 and v2 stay as the broad set. The TGLF
labelling job is approved as usual.
(2) Median relative error of the ensemble mean at most 0.30 on Q~e~ and on Q~i~, on cases with
|Q| above 1 gyro-Bohm unit, on each machine's v3 held-out split. Errors on the v1 split are
reported, not gated; the closed-loop error is checked at M4.
(3) Q~e~ and Q~i~ get a ReLU at the output: exactly zero below threshold, never negative. The
particle fluxes keep their sign. Training must not let the ReLU block gradients for points
predicted stable (a linear output in training with a penalty on positive predictions where
TGLF's flux is not positive, clipped in use, as QLKNN does). Setting TGLF's negative heat fluxes
to zero is a cost, to be listed as a ceiling. Monotonicity is measured on TGLF scans before it
is imposed.

### OQ-18 · Close M2 without active learning, QuaLiKiz and the gated-code drivers? {#oq-18}

*Decided 3 Oct 2026.* M2's three acceptance criteria were met on the two version 1 datasets,
but three of its tasks were not built: active learning near the critical gradients, a QuaLiKiz
driver, and drivers for the gated (Tier B) codes. **Decision.** (a) Active learning moves to M3:
it needs a model of where the thresholds are, and the M3 ensembles provide one; the new points
become dataset version 2, v1 unchanged. (b) QuaLiKiz is deferred: its shifted-circle geometry
does not represent the MAST-U shapes, and QLKNN already serves the conventional case. (c) A
driver interface with stubs for the gated codes, which refuse to run without access, was built.
M2 closed ([M2 page](milestones/M2.qmd)). For M3 the owner set: train on every case, with the
fluxes in a sign-preserving log space and no filtering; one ensemble per machine; training on
GPUs, each cluster job approved; the accuracy target to be set after a first baseline
([entry 18](log/18-tglf-surrogates-baseline.qmd)).

### OQ-16 · Kinetic ranges, ITER shapes and the α~MHD~ cap for the M2 datasets {#oq-16}

*Decided 2 Oct 2026.* The owner set one dataset per machine, MAST-U and ITER. The geometry
ranges were measured ([OQ-15](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-15)); the kinetic ranges, the ion species and a cap on the normalised
pressure gradient α~MHD~ were proposed by the agent from memory and needed a decision before
any data was generated. Three questions: (a) do the kinetic ranges and ions stand per machine;
(b) is one ITER plasma shape with the current ramp-up's q profiles enough, or should 15 MA
baseline equilibria be added first; (c) a fixed cap, a cap that depends on the magnetic shear,
or sampling α~MHD~ in place of β~e~.

**Decision.** (a) Approved as proposed for both machines: D and carbon for MAST-U, D-T as one
ion of mean mass and neon for ITER (ranges in [datasets](technical/datasets.qmd#sampling-space)).
(b) One shape is enough for version 1; the missing baseline is recorded as a limit ([K-016](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-016)) and
baseline shapes come before an ITER version 2. (c) Fixed caps for version 1 (MAST-U 4, ITER 2),
a shear-dependent cap to follow ([K-017](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-017)). The two datasets were generated the same day
([entry 17](log/17-tglf-datasets-mastu-iter.qmd)).

### OQ-15 · Sampling ranges and TGLF settings for MAST-U {#oq-15}

*Decided 2 Oct 2026.* MAST-U is outside both surrogates TORAX ships with (aspect ratio fixed at
3, or elongation up to 1.5). The agent proposed ranges from memory, not checked against a
source. **Decision:** the agent measures the geometry ranges on equilibria rather than choosing
them, and the kinetic ranges go to a physics check (became [OQ-16](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-16)); a second region besides
MAST-U, each tagged so it can be selected alone or pooled (became the ITER dataset); TGLF with
the SAT2 saturation rule and both magnetic perturbations; CGYRO spot checks of TGLF at M4.

interior surfaces at most 0.24, not 0.6).

### M1 physicist review {#m1-review}

*Passed 1 Oct 2026.* The last M1 acceptance criterion is a review by a physicist. The owner did
the review as reviewer of record. The agent set out six items, each with its evidence and a
recommendation; **the owner accepted all six recommendations as written.**

1. **Benchmark tolerance**, against RAPTOR on the published ITER L-mode case ([OQ-12](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-12)): the
   t = 10 s profiles within 2% for T~i~, T~e~, ψ and q, and within 0.1% for the densities; the
   line-averaged temperature and density traces within 5% over 0–10 s. The fusion and Ohmic
   powers are reported, not gated: the paper's two codes differ by 13–22% on the alpha
   ion/electron split. Result at the published settings: [T_i 1.23% (1.1%), T_e 0.28% (0.71%), n_e 0.03% (0.03%), psi 0.49% (0.41%), q 0.69% (0.70%)]{.claim}[C-050](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-050){.cid .st-reviewed}; transient
   [2.4% at dt = 0.05 s, 2.9% at dt = 0.00625 s (1.0% at t = 10 s)]{.claim}[C-053](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-053){.cid .st-reviewed}. Both pass.
2. **TORAX version.** The differences between the paper's TORAX run and TORAX 1.4.3
   ([T_i 0.13%, T_e 0.50%, n_e 0.01%, psi 0.08%, q 0.16%; Ohmic power density 3.6%]{.claim}[C-051](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-051){.cid .st-reviewed}) are accepted as a code-version effect.
3. **Pedestal.** The fixed-pedestal model's pinning source removes [87–98%]{.claim}[C-038](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-038){.cid .st-reviewed} of the
   heating in the ITER hybrid ramp-up. Accepted for core profiles inside ρ = 0.9; power
   crossing the edge is not taken from these runs ([K-010](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-010)). Revisited at M3.
4. **Time step.** The ITER hybrid example settings are not converged in time ([entry
   3](log/03-fixed-step-loop.qmd)). They are used only to check the wrapper. Runs used as a
   physics reference use a step at which halving it changes the core temperature by at most 1%
   after the first 5 s. Solver stalls stay reported ([OQ-5](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-5)).
5. **ASCOT5 alpha source.** Orbit tolerance 10^-7^ ([0.348 at 10^-6^, 0.331 at 10^-7^]{.claim}[C-058](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-058){.cid .st-reviewed} of the birth power to
   ions at 10^-6^ and 10^-7^); 640 markers give the total ([72.2 MW vs 70.5 MW]{.claim}[C-059](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-059){.cid .st-reviewed} against TORAX's
   local model) and the electron/ion split, and the radial shape waits for the production run
   ([OQ-13](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-13)). Holding the source fixed for 2 s is accepted ([+0.03% in stored energy (central T_e +0.5%, T_e and T_i profiles 0.6%)]{.claim}[C-060](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-060){.cid .st-reviewed}). The small excess
   in the markers' birth power ([K-011](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-011)) is to be explained before neutral-beam ions are added.
6. **Fallback, pedestal and sawtooth models**: [OQ-1](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-1) below.

The claims these items judged are marked *reviewed* in the [claims register](claims.qmd).

### OQ-1 · The fallback transport model {#oq-1}

*Decided 1 Oct 2026, at the M1 physicist review.* M0 needed a toy transport model to exercise
the loop, and a smooth critical-gradient form was used. **The trusted fallback for real runs is
TORAX's Bohm/gyro-Bohm model**, which is already the fallback behind the guard inside TORAX. The
critical-gradient form stays as the closure of the Tokamak Toolkit's own analytic test loop only. For M1 the
pedestal is TORAX's fixed pedestal, and sawtooth mixing is represented by a constant
diffusivity near the axis (the ITER examples have no sawtooth model); a sawtooth model is added
when a case needs one.

### OQ-13 · A third ASCOT5 job, for the production run {#oq-13}

*Decided 1 Oct 2026.* The second ASCOT5 job ([entry 12](log/12-ascot5-second-run.qmd)) finished
its tolerance check but not its production run: a per-marker time limit, set too short by the
agent, stopped [2823 of 6400 markers, 18% of the birth power]{.claim}[C-057](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-057){.cid .st-measured}. **A third job is approved**: up to eight hours on one node,
the production run at the tighter tolerance with no time limit, and a check at a tighter one
still. The M1 physicist review is not held for it.

*Outcome, 2 Oct 2026* ([entry 15](log/15-ascot5-production-run.qmd)). The job ran in 3 h 37 min
and every alpha finished. Total heating: [71.8 MW vs 70.5 MW]{.claim}[C-064](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-064){.cid .st-measured}. The tighter check changed the
heating by [electrons -0.16%, ions +0.08%]{.claim}[C-066](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-066){.cid .st-measured}, so the working tolerance stands. No further job is requested.

### OQ-12 · Which published profiles the benchmark is compared with {#oq-12}

*Decided 1 Oct 2026.* M1 asks for a match to *published profiles*. The ITER hybrid scenarios
have no published profiles from a second code. The TORAX paper publishes one quantitative
comparison with an independent code, RAPTOR, on an ITER L-mode case, with its full
configuration and the profiles as vector figures. **That case is the M1 physics benchmark**,
compared with both RAPTOR's and the paper's own TORAX curves, first at the published time step
and then at a converged one ([entry 11](log/11-raptor-lmode-benchmark.qmd)). The ITER hybrid
runs remain the stiff-transport and pedestal case. The tolerance was set at the
[M1 physicist review](#m1-review).

### OQ-11 · A second ASCOT5 cluster job {#oq-11}

*Decided 1 Oct 2026.* The first ASCOT5 job ([entry 10](log/10-ascot5-alpha-heating.qmd))
showed that the orbit tolerance chosen for speed loses alphas that should be confined ([C-043](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-043)),
and that at the tighter tolerance 640 markers resolve the total alpha heating but not its
radial shape ([C-045](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-045)). **A second job is approved**: one node for up to four hours, ten times
more markers at the tighter tolerance, and a check at a tighter one still. Further jobs need
their own approval. Outcome: [entry 12](log/12-ascot5-second-run.qmd) and [OQ-13](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-13).

### OQ-10 · Which radial variable the guard's features use {#oq-10}

*Deferred 1 Oct 2026, to M3.* The guard checks whether a plasma state is inside the region the
surrogate was trained on, using features such as normalised temperature gradients. The Tokamak Toolkit
computes those gradients with respect to the normalised flux radius, scaled by the geometric
minor radius; QLKNN, as TORAX feeds it, uses the midplane minor radius of each surface. On the
ITER hybrid scenario the two differ from [+19%]{.claim}[C-032](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-032){.cid .st-measured} in the core to about a third at the
edge ([K-008](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-008)). No run is affected yet. **The convention will be chosen when the first trained
surrogate exists (M3)**, and in any case before a verified domain is certified (M4).

### OQ-9 · Fast-ion sources from ASCOT5 {#oq-9}

*Decided 1 Oct 2026.* **Fusion alphas first**, born from the plasma profiles TORAX computes, as
a direct check against TORAX's own alpha heating. Neutral-beam ions follow once a physicist has
approved the injector geometry. **One short test job on the compute cluster is approved**; each
further job needs its own approval.

### OQ-5 · What "reproduces the benchmark" means {#oq-5}

*Decided 1 Oct 2026.* Two comparisons: the Tokamak Toolkit's loop against TORAX's own output at the same
settings (a check of the wrapper), and against the published cross-code comparison (a physics
statement). **The wrapper check must agree to 10^-10^** (it passes at round-off: [C-006](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-006), [C-007](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-007)).
**The physics tolerance is set by the physicist reviewer** at the M1 gate (set: see the
[M1 physicist review](#m1-review)). Because the published
reference runs are not converged in time ([entry 3](log/03-fixed-step-loop.qmd), [C-012](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-012), [C-013](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-013)),
**the physics comparison is made at the published settings first**, then at a converged time
step, with the difference reported as its own line in the discrepancy budget. **Solver stalls
stay reported**, not tuned away by relaxing a line-search setting
([entry 5](log/05-stalls-rf-and-builds.qmd), [C-011](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-011)). **Energy and particles must balance to
10^-6^ per step** on converged steps ([entry 8](log/08-energy-particle-balance.qmd), [C-035](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-035), [C-036](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-036)); the
flat-top reference solver's defect ([C-037](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-037)) is reported, not required to close.

### OQ-3 · Where the code will live {#oq-3}

*Decided 1 Oct 2026.* **A private hosted repository**, where the continuous-integration
workflow runs on every change. The code stays private; this log is how the work is shown. Until
the workflow has passed, "tested" in the [claims register](claims.qmd) still means "asserted by
a named test, run before each publish".

### OQ-8 · Which machine description for the equilibrium solver {#oq-8}

*Decided 30 Sep 2026.* **MAST-U.** FreeGSNKE's repository already ships a MAST-U-like machine
description (coils, passive structures, limiter, wall; credited to UKAEA) under the same open
licence, so nothing had to be assembled from published drawings. It is fetched from a pinned
upstream version with a checksum per file. This covers the equilibrium work only: the M1
transport benchmark stays with the ITER scenario, because no published TORAX MAST-U scenario
exists and QLKNN was not trained on spherical-tokamak conditions.

### OQ-7 · Input data for a STEP extension {#oq-7}

*Deferred 30 Sep 2026.* Extending the benchmark to a STEP power-plant flat-top is a future
extension, not part of M1. The work stays with the ITER benchmark and MAST-U for now; the data
question reopens if and when the extension is picked up.

### OQ-6 · Which benchmark {#oq-6}

*Decided 21 Sep 2026, amended 30 Sep 2026.* **The ITER hybrid scenario** that ships with
TORAX: an 80-second current ramp-up, and a 5-second flat-top as the quicker check. A planned
STEP extension was deferred on 30 Sep ([OQ-7](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-7)).

### OQ-4 · Newton-Raphson for the coupling loop {#oq-4}

*Decided 21 Sep 2026.* **Approved.** The M0 loop used relaxed Picard iteration, which
oscillates instead of converging once transport becomes stiff: on the toy model's original
settings the residual sat between 3 × 10⁻² and 8 × 10⁻² after 12 iterations. The owner
approved a Newton-Raphson solver with derivatives from automatic differentiation and a fixed
iteration count, keeping Picard as the fallback, and stall reporting for both
([entry 1](log/01-newton-solver.qmd)).

### OQ-2 · Where to run {#oq-2}

*Decided 21 Sep 2026.* Tests and the early milestones run on an interactive node with one
datacentre GPU. Anything longer goes through the cluster's batch system on an allocation the
owner named, and every job is announced to the owner before it is submitted.

The corrected original ITER numerical pilot completes with readable native
heating and signed-current profiles ([the corrected EC reference completes in 83.16 s with readable native profiles]{.claim}[C-156](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-156){.cid .st-measured}). Native accounting
and descriptive saved-reference comparisons are retained; the rendered
PostScript page is blank. Production EC coupling contracts, grouped sampling
and ITER boundary choices remain open.
